> AGENT

Task #242 (TagsInput agnostic core) is implemented, audited, and ready for your review.

## What was built

**New component:** [crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs](crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs) — the framework-agnostic `TagsInput` state machine (State/Event/Context/Props/`BlurBehavior`/Messages/`Effect`/Part/Machine/Api), registered in [selection/mod.rs](crates/ars-components/src/selection/mod.rs).

**Tests** (all passing): 100 inline unit + snapshot tests, 1 `#[ignore]` proptest (3000 cases), 1 spec-conformance anatomy test — covering every named acceptance test from the issue: add on Enter/comma, remove via button/Backspace, arrow navigation, duplicate prevention, max limit, validation (`invalid`/ARIA/ErrorMessage), grid `listbox`/grid ARIA, per-tag remove button, input attrs, multi-value hidden input, plus inline editing, paste, IME, blur behavior, and announcements.

## Spec drift resolved in this PR (per spec-sync rule)

The spec's §1.6 code couldn't be implemented verbatim. Amended [spec/components/selection/tags-input.md](spec/components/selection/tags-input.md):
1. **Typed `Effect` enum** (`FocusTag`/`FocusInput`/`FocusEditInput`/`Announce`) replacing the spec's `use_platform_effects()` calls — agnostic core can't call adapter functions; matches the `pin_input` convention (adapter resolves focus from `ctx`).
2. **Deduplicated** the `Api` event-handler methods (spec defined them twice — wouldn't compile).
3. **`editing_draft`** wired into Context (your choice: full inline-edit ownership).
4. **`LiveRegion` part + `Messages` + `Announce` effect** for screen-reader announcements (your choice).
5. **Delimiter-on-type** splitting in `InputChange` (the issue's "add on comma" test + IME note required it; spec only split on paste).
6. §2 anatomy, §3.1/§3.3, §4.1, §6.2 brought into line with the implementation.

## Audit findings (all landed)
- **Phase 1:** §6.2 parity table used non-existent `Item*` part names → fixed to real anatomy; §3.1 `aria-describedby`→`aria-description` for Tag.
- **Phase 2** (2 clean rounds): adapter specs/manifest/catalog already consistent; no doctest needed (sibling selection components have none).
- **Phase 3:** coverage 89.6% → **97.5% line**; removed one dead `!props.editable` guard in `CommitEdit` (unreachable — `EditingTag` requires `editable` and props are immutable); added tests for the remaining real gaps. Also hardened the machine (proptest-discovered): list-mutating events are ignored during `EditingTag`, and `CommitEdit`/`CancelEdit` outside editing are rejected, so focus/edit indices never dangle.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p ars-components --features i18n --all-targets` — 5098 + 121 pass, 0 fail
- `cargo test -p ars-components --lib` (default features) — pass
- `cargo clippy -p ars-components --all-targets --features i18n` and `--workspace` — 0 warnings
- `cargo fmt --check` — clean; `cargo doc` — my module is warning-free
- `cargo xtask spec validate` + `compile-snippets` — pass; `insta --unreferenced=reject` — no orphans

Not yet run (per workflow): `cargo xci-fast` runs after your approval, before push. Adapter components (Leptos/Dioxus), widgets examples, and E2E are out of scope for this agnostic-core task.

When `value` is `Some`, this prop puts the machine in controlled mode, but `Props` has no `on_value_change`/equivalent callback and `Machine` does not override `on_props_changed` to sync later prop updates. Because `Bindable::get()` keeps returning the controlled value while transitions only call `ctx.value.set(...)` internally, controlled consumers cannot add, remove, clear, or edit tags through the connect API and also are not notified of the next value to round-trip.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GzAI2
FILE crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:1317  (replyTo databaseId=3349698195)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not rely on a hidden input for required validation**

When `required` is set and the tag list is empty, this adds `required` to an `<input type="hidden">`, but hidden inputs do not participate in browser constraint validation, so a required TagsInput can still submit with no tags. MDN documents that hidden inputs are excluded from constraint validation and that `required` is not supported on the hidden input type: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/hidden#validation

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GzAI-
FILE crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:1437  (replyTo databaseId=3349698204)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Delete clicked duplicate tags by index**

When `allow_duplicates(true)` is used, clicking one tag's delete trigger sends `RemoveTag(value)`, and that transition filters out every tag with the same value. In a list like `["a", "a", "b"]`, deleting either visible `a` chip removes both chips, unlike keyboard deletion which uses `RemoveTagAtIndex(index)` and removes only the focused chip.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GzAJF
FILE crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:1425  (replyTo databaseId=3349698211)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Send Escape on a tag back to the input**

When focus is on any tag except the last one, pressing Escape currently dispatches `FocusNextTag`, so it moves focus to the next tag instead of deselecting the tag list. The spec's keyboard table says Escape on a tag should focus the input, so a list like `["a", "b"]` leaves keyboard users trapped on `b` after pressing Escape on `a`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GzAJL
FILE crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:1462  (replyTo databaseId=3349698218)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Commit inline edits on Tab instead of discarding them**

During inline editing, the spec says Tab commits the edit and then moves focus onward, but this handler only handles Enter and Escape; Tab falls through to `_ => {}`. In the browser the focus then leaves the edit input and the `Blur` transition for `EditingTag` discards `editing_draft`, so users who tab away after editing lose their change.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GzAJP
FILE crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:1402  (replyTo databaseId=3349698226)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor ArrowLeft at the start of non-empty input**

The spec's keyboard table says ArrowLeft should focus the last tag when the input caret is at the start, but this handler only does so when `input_value` is empty. As a result, a user who has typed text, moves the caret to position 0, and presses ArrowLeft cannot navigate back into the tag list by keyboard.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GzAJW
FILE crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:596  (replyTo databaseId=3349698233)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Block delimiter changes while disabled or read-only**

This disabled/readonly guard omits `InputChange` and `Blur`, but both can mutate the tag list: `InputChange("b,")` takes the delimiter-splitting path and appends `b`, and `InputChange("b")` followed by `Blur` commits the pending tag. That means a disabled or read-only machine can still add tags through normal transition events even though the guard claims mutating events are rejected.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GzAJZ
FILE crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:1390  (replyTo databaseId=3349698238)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Suppress key actions when the event is composing**

This only checks the stored context flag, but `KeyboardEventData` also carries `is_composing`; if an Enter keydown arrives with `data.is_composing == true` before the composition-start event has updated context, the handler still dispatches `AddTag`. Other input components check the event flag directly, and the interaction contract requires suppressing character-driven actions while the keyboard event is composing.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply max_length to inline tag edits**

`max_length` is documented as the maximum character length per tag, but the inline edit input never receives a `maxlength` attribute and `CommitEdit` does not enforce the limit. With `editable(true).max_length(3)`, a user can edit an existing tag to `abcdef` even though new-tag entry is constrained.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Synchronize copied props after set_props**

These props are copied into `Context` only during initialization, and the machine does not override `on_props_changed`; after a parent changes `disabled`, `readonly`, or `max`, the connect attrs and transition guards keep using the old context values. For example, setting `disabled` after mount leaves the root without disabled attrs and still allows tag mutations.

    fn on_props_changed(old: &Props, new: &Props) -> Vec<Event> {
        assert_eq!(
            old.id, new.id,
            "text_field::Props.id must remain stable after init"
        );

        let mut events = Vec::new();

        if old.value != new.value {
            events.push(Event::SetValue(new.value.clone()));
        }

        if props_output_changed(old, new) {
            events.push(Event::SetProps);
        }

        events
    }

952	/// Builds the plan for an [`Event::AddTag`], including the max-reached announcement.
953	fn add_tag_plan(ctx: &Context, tag: &str) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {
954	    let trimmed = tag.trim().to_string();
955	
956	    if trimmed.is_empty() {
957	        return None;
958	    }
959	
960	    if let Some(max) = ctx.max.filter(|&max| ctx.value.get().len() >= max) {
961	        let announcement = (ctx.messages.max_reached_announcement)(max, &ctx.locale);
962	
963	        return Some(
964	            TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
965	                ctx.live_message = announcement;
966	            })
967	            .with_effect(PendingEffect::named(Effect::Announce)),
968	        );
969	    }
970	
971	    if !ctx.allow_duplicates && ctx.value.get().contains(&trimmed) {
972	        return None;
973	    }
974	
975	    Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
976	        let mut tags = ctx.value.get().clone();
977	
978	        tags.push(trimmed);
979	
980	        ctx.value.set(tags);
981	        ctx.input_value.clear();
982	        ctx.focused_tag = None;
983	    }))
984	}
985	
986	/// Builds the plan for removing the tag `value` (first found at `removed_index`),
987	/// updating focus and emitting the removal announcement.
988	fn remove_plan(
989	    ctx: &Context,
990	    removed_index: Option<usize>,
991	    value: &str,
992	) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {
993	    let removed_index = removed_index?;
994	
995	    let new_tags = ctx
996	        .value
997	        .get()
998	        .iter()
999	        .filter(|tag| tag.as_str() != value)
1000	        .cloned()
1001	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
1002	
1003	    let will_be_empty = new_tags.is_empty();
1004	
1005	    let announcement = (ctx.messages.removed_announcement)(value, &ctx.locale);
1006	
1007	    let focus_effect = if will_be_empty {
1008	        Effect::FocusInput
1009	    } else {
1010	        Effect::FocusTag
1011	    };
1012	
1013	    Some(
1014	        TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
1015	            let focused_tag = (!new_tags.is_empty()).then(|| removed_index.min(new_tags.len() - 1));
1016	
1017	            ctx.value.set(new_tags);
1018	            ctx.focused_tag = focused_tag;
1019	            ctx.live_message = announcement;
1020	        })
1021	        .with_effect(PendingEffect::named(focus_effect))
1022	        .with_effect(PendingEffect::named(Effect::Announce)),
1023	    )
1024	}

Reads `Context::value` at effect-run time (post-apply), so it reports\n/// the new value even in controlled mode where `get()` still returns the parent's.\nfn value_change_effect() -> PendingEffect<Machine> {\n    PendingEffect::new(Effect::ValueChange, |ctx: &Context, props: &Props, _send| {\n        if let Some(callback) = &props.on_value_change {\n            callback(ctx.value.pending().clone());\n        }\n\n        no_cleanup()\n    })\n}\n\n/// Returns `true` when an output-affecting prop changed and the context must be\n/// re-synchronized via [`Event::SetProps`].\nfn props_output_changed(old: &Props, new: &Props) -> bool {\n    old.disabled != new.disabled\n        || old.readonly != new.readonly\n        || old.invalid != new.invalid\n        || old.max != new.max\n        || old.max_length != new.max_length\n        || old.delimiter != new.delimiter\n        || old.add_on_paste != new.add_on_paste\n        || old.allow_duplicates != new.allow_duplicates\n        || old.blur_behavior != new.blur_behavior\n        || old.required != new.required\n        || old.placeholder != new.placeholder\n        || old.name != new.name\n        || old.editable != new.editable\n}"

spec's keyboard table.\n    pub fn on_input_keydown(&self, data: &KeyboardEventData, caret_at_start: bool) {\n        // Suppress character-driven actions while composing — check both the stored\n        // context flag and the event's own flag, since an Enter keydown can arrive\n        // mid-composition before the composition-start event updates the context.\n        if self.ctx.is_composing || data.is_composing {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        match data.key {\n            KeyboardKey::Enter => {\n                if !self.ctx.input_value.trim().is_empty() {\n                    (self.send)(Event::AddTag(self.ctx.input_value.clone()));\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Backspace deletes back into the tags only when there is nothing left\n            // to delete in the input.\n            KeyboardKey::Backspace => {\n                if self.ctx.input_value.is_empty() {\n                    (self.send)(Event::FocusPrevTag);\n                }\n            }\n\n            // ArrowLeft navigates into the tag list when the caret is at the start.\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft => {\n                if caret_at_start {\n                    (self.send)(Event::FocusPrevTag);\n                }\n            }\n\n            KeyboardKey::Escape => {\n                (self.send)(Event::InputChange(String::new()));\n            }\n\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Handle a keydown on a focused tag at `index`.\n    pub fn on_tag_keydown(&self, index: usize, data: &KeyboardEventData) {\n        match data.key {\n (self.send)(Event::FocusPrevTag),\n\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowRight => (self.send)(Event::FocusNextTag),\n\n            // Escape deselects the tag list and returns focus to the input,\n (self.send)(Event::EditTag { index });\n            }\n\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Handle a click on a tag's delete trigger at `index`.\n    ///\n    /// Removes by index (not by value) so that, with duplicates allowed, clicking\n    /// one chip removes only that chip — matching keyboard deletion.\n    pub fn on_tag_delete(&self, index: usize) {\n        (self.send)(Event::RemoveTagAtIndex(index));\n    }"

  "old_string": "/// Builds the plan for removing the tag `value` (first found at `removed_index`),\n/// updating focus and emitting the removal announcement.\nfn remove_plan(\n    ctx: &Context,\n    removed_index: Option<usize>,\n    value: &str,\n) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {\n    let removed_index = removed_index?;\n\n    let new_tags = ctx\n        .value\n        .get()\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|tag| tag.as_str() != value)\n        .cloned()\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n\n    let will_be_empty = new_tags.is_empty();\n\n    let announcement = (ctx.messages.removed_announcement)(value, &ctx.locale);\n\n    let focus_effect = if will_be_empty {\n        Effect::FocusInput\n    } else {\n        Effect::FocusTag\n    };\n\n    Some(\n        TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n            let focused_tag = (!new_tags.is_empty()).then(|| removed_index.min(new_tags.len() - 1));\n\n            ctx.value.set(new_tags);\n            ctx.focused_tag = focused_tag;\n            ctx.live_message = announcement;\n        })\n        .with_effect(PendingEffect::named(focus_effect))\n        .with_effect(PendingEffect::named(Effect::Announce))\n        .with_effect(value_change_effect()),\n    )\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Builds the plan for removing exactly the tag at `index`, updating focus and\n/// emitting the removal announcement. Removing by index (rather than filtering by\n/// value) ensures that with duplicates allowed only the targeted chip is removed.\nfn remove_plan(ctx: &Context, index: usize) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {\n    let current = ctx.value.get();\n\n    let value = current.get(index)?.clone();\n\n    let mut new_tags = current.clone();\n    new_tags.remove(index);\n\n    let will_be_empty = new_tags.is_empty();\n\n    let announcement = (ctx.messages.removed_announcement)(&value, &ctx.locale);\n\n    let focus_effect = if will_be_empty {\n        Effect::FocusInput\n    } else {\n        Effect::FocusTag\n    };\n\n    Some(\n        TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n            let focused_tag = (!new_tags.is_empty()).then(|| index.min(new_tags.len() - 1));\n\n            ctx.value.set(new_tags);\n            ctx.focused_tag = focused_tag;\n            ctx.live_message = announcement;\n        })\n        .with_effect(PendingEffect::named(focus_effect))\n        .with_effect(PendingEffect::named(Effect::Announce))\n        .with_effect(value_change_effect()),\n    )\n}"
}

  "old_string": "    /// Handle a keydown on an inline-edit input at `index`.\n    pub fn on_tag_edit_keydown(&self, index: usize, data: &KeyboardEventData) {\n        match data.key {\n            KeyboardKey::Enter => (self.send)(Event::CommitEdit {\n                index,\n                value: self.ctx.editing_draft.clone(),\n            }),\n\n            KeyboardKey::Escape => (self.send)(Event::CancelEdit),\n\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }",
  "new_string": "    /// Handle a keydown on an inline-edit input at `index`.\n    pub fn on_tag_edit_keydown(&self, index: usize, data: &KeyboardEventData) {\n        match data.key {\n            // Enter and Tab both commit the edit (Tab additionally lets the browser\n            // move focus onward); committing first avoids losing the draft to the\n            // `EditingTag` blur, which discards it.\n            KeyboardKey::Enter | KeyboardKey::Tab => (self.send)(Event::CommitEdit {\n                index,\n                value: self.ctx.editing_draft.clone(),\n            }),\n\n            KeyboardKey::Escape => (self.send)(Event::CancelEdit),\n\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }"
}

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G0Zbz | reply=3350198322 | crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:1397
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the pending input value in input_attrs**

When the user adds a tag with Enter or by typing the delimiter, the transition clears `ctx.input_value`, but this input never receives a `value` attribute from the connect API. Adapters that render from `input_attrs()` therefore cannot drive the DOM input back to `""`, so the just-added text can remain visible and be reused on the next edit; the new-tag input should expose `HtmlAttr::Value` from `ctx.input_value` like the other controlled input parts do.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G0Zb1 | reply=3350198325 | crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:814
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply max_length when adding on blur**

For `BlurBehavior::Add`, this guard allows any non-empty pending input through as long as the tag count and duplicate checks pass. With `max_length` set, an over-limit value that is correctly rejected by Enter, paste, and inline-edit commit is still appended when the input blurs, violating the per-tag length cap for users who tab/click away after typing.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G0Zb6 | reply=3350198330 | crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:920
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear stale tag indices after controlled value sync**

When a controlled parent replaces the value with a shorter list while a tag is focused or being edited, `SetValue` only updates the bindable value and leaves `focused_tag`, `editing_tag`, and possibly `State::EditingTag { index }` pointing at the old index. That makes subsequent focus effects/attrs target a non-existent tag and breaks the invariant that these indices refer to real tags; clamp or clear the focus/edit state when the new controlled value no longer contains the indexed tag.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G0ZcC | reply=3350198338 | crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:1350
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve button semantics for tag delete triggers**

When the adapter follows the anatomy table and spreads `tag_delete_trigger_attrs()` onto a `<button>`, this explicit `role="gridcell"` overrides the native button role, so screen-reader users get a grid cell instead of a remove button. Put the gridcell role on a wrapper cell or keep the trigger itself as a button so the labelled removal control remains exposed as an interactive button.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G0ZcF | reply=3350198343 | crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:1453
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Set non-submit type on trigger buttons**

In forms, a `<button>` without `type` defaults to submit, and the anatomy declares `ClearTrigger` (and `TagDeleteTrigger`) as buttons. As a result, clicking clear-all or a per-tag remove trigger can submit the surrounding form while mutating the tag list; these action triggers should emit `HtmlAttr::Type = "button"` like the other component trigger attrs in the workspace.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G0ZcK | reply=3350198349 | crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:1375
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disable the inline edit input when props disable editing**

If the component is disabled or made read-only while a tag is already in edit mode, `SetProps` updates `ctx.disabled`/`ctx.readonly` but the visible `TagEdit` input still receives neither `disabled` nor `readonly`. The DOM input remains operable even though the state machine now drops `InputChange`/`CommitEdit`, causing typed text to be accepted by the browser and then ignored by the component; mirror the disabled/read-only attrs here as `input_attrs()` does.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G0ZcO | reply=3350198355 | crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:1386
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Actually hide inactive edit inputs**

For every tag that is not being edited, this only emits a styling data attribute while leaving a text `<input>` otherwise focusable and exposed. If adapters render the `TagEdit` part for each tag as the anatomy describes, keyboard and screen-reader users can still reach these inactive edit inputs unless CSS happens to remove them; emit a real `hidden`/`aria-hidden` plus non-focusable state, or have the API make non-editing inputs safe by default.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G0ZcR | reply=3350198359 | crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:1605
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reverse tag arrow navigation in RTL locales**

The spec says horizontal tag order is RTL-aware, but these handlers always map Left to previous and Right to next. In an RTL locale, users pressing the visually-forward arrow on a focused tag will move backward (and ArrowLeft from the input is the only way back into the list), unlike the repo's other selection components that resolve direction before dispatching arrow navigation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G0ZcU | reply=3350198362 | crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:765
**<sub><sub>![P3 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P3-lightgrey?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid value-change callbacks for rejected edits**

When an inline edit is rejected because the new value is a duplicate or exceeds `max_length`, the original tag list is left unchanged but this transition still emits `ValueChange`. In those scenarios `on_value_change` receives the unchanged list even though the public contract says it fires when the tag list changes, which can make controlled parents run change logic or validation for an edit that was not committed.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/ericson/Workspace/Rust/ars-ui.worktrees/impl-242/crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs",
  "old_string": "            Event::SetValue(value) => {\n                let value = value.clone();\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n                    if let Some(value) = value {\n                        ctx.value.set(value.clone());\n                        ctx.value.sync_controlled(Some(value));\n                    } else {\n                        ctx.value.sync_controlled(None);\n                    }\n                }))\n            }",
  "new_string": "            Event::SetValue(value) => {\n                let value = value.clone();\n\n                // Post-sync length, used to clamp stale focus/edit indices and to\n                // exit an inline edit whose tag the new value no longer contains.\n                let new_len = match &value {\n                    Some(new_value) => new_value.len(),\n                    None => ctx.value.pending().len(),\n                };\n                let exit_editing =\n                    matches!(state, State::EditingTag { index } if *index >= new_len);\n\n                let plan = if exit_editing {\n                    TransitionPlan::to(State::Focused)\n                } else {\n                    TransitionPlan::new()\n                };\n\n                Some(plan.apply(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n                    if let Some(value) = value {\n                        ctx.value.set(value.clone());\n                        ctx.value.sync_controlled(Some(value));\n                    } else {\n                        ctx.value.sync_controlled(None);\n                    }\n\n                    // A controlled parent may replace the list with a shorter one;\n                    // never let focus/edit indices point past the end.\n                    let len = ctx.value.get().len();\n                    if ctx.focused_tag.is_some_and(|index| index >= len) {\n                        ctx.focused_tag = None;\n                    }\n                    if ctx.editing_tag.is_some_and(|index| index >= len) {\n                        ctx.editing_tag = None;\n                        ctx.editing_draft.clear();\n                    }\n                }))\n            }"
}

.iter()\n                                .enumerate()\n                                .any(|(other, tag)| other != index && tag == &trimmed);\n                        let replaces_with_new = tags[index] != trimmed;\n                        !is_duplicate && !exceeds_max_length(max_length, &trimmed) && replaces_with_new\n                    });\n\n                let mut plan = TransitionPlan::to(State::Focused)\n                    .apply(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n                        let mut tags = ctx.value.get().clone();\n\n                        if index < tags.len() {\n                            if trimmed.is_empty() {\n                                tags.remove(index);\n                            } else {\n                                let is_duplicate = !allow_duplicates\n                                    && tags\n                                        .iter()\n                                        .enumerate()\n                                        .any(|(other, tag)| other != index && tag == &trimmed);\n\n                                // Reject duplicates and over-length edits: keep the\n                                // original tag rather than committing an invalid value.\n                                if !is_duplicate && !exceeds_max_length(max_length, &trimmed) {\n                                    tags[index] = trimmed;\n                                }\n                            }\n\n                            ctx.value.set(tags);\n                        }\n\n                        ctx.editing_tag = None;\n                        ctx.editing_draft.clear();\n                    })\n                    .with_effect(PendingEffect::named(Effect::FocusInput));\n\n                if changes {\n                    plan = plan.with_effect(value_change_effect());\n                }\n\n                Some(plan)\n            }"
}

          (self.send)(Event::RemoveTagAtIndex(index));\n            }\n\n            // Horizontal arrows resolve against text direction: in RTL the visually\n            // forward arrow (ArrowLeft) (self.send)(Event::FocusPrevTag);\n                } else {\n                    (self.send)(Event::FocusNextTag);\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Escape deselects the tag list and toward the previous tag,\n    /// accounting for RTL text direction (where ArrowRight moves backward).\n    fn is_toward_prev(&self, key: KeyboardKey) -> bool {\n        match self.ctx.dir {\n            Direction::Rtl => key == KeyboardKey::ArrowRight,\n            Direction::Ltr => key == KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft,\n        }\n    }"

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1GlU | reply=3350449597 | crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:754
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Re-check editable before committing edits**

If a parent turns `editable` off while a tag is already in `EditingTag`, this arm still accepts `CommitEdit` and can overwrite or remove the tag. `Service::set_props` updates `props` live, and `editable` is deliberately excluded from `SetProps`, so this scenario is not prevented elsewhere; the spec guard also says `CommitEdit` is rejected when `editable: false`. Guard this path against `!props.editable` or exit edit mode when the prop changes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1GlX | reply=3350449600 | crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:1159
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid value-change effects when no tag was added**

When delimiter splitting runs but every segment is rejected by `push_if_allowed` (for example typing `a,` when `a` already exists, or when the max count is already reached), this still queues `ValueChange` after setting the unchanged tag list. Since `Props::on_value_change` is documented to fire only when the tag list changes, controlled parents receive spurious callbacks with the same value; track whether any segment was appended before attaching this effect.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1GlZ | reply=3350449604 | crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:1063
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve pending controlled edits across rapid changes**

In controlled mode, `Bindable::get()` keeps returning the parent value until the callback is round-tripped through `set_props`, so building the next list from `get()` here drops any pending internal edit. For example, with controlled value `["a"]`, two add events for `b` then `c` before the parent re-renders produce callbacks `["a","b"]` then `["a","c"]`, losing `b`; use the pending value as the base for controlled mutations that report through `on_value_change`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1Gld | reply=3350449609 | crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:1737
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve auto direction before arrow handling**

When consumers pass `Direction::Auto` under an RTL locale, this falls into the LTR branch, so ArrowRight no longer enters the tag list from the input and focused-tag ArrowLeft/ArrowRight behavior is reversed from the documented RTL behavior. Other components resolve `Auto` from `ctx.locale.direction()` before keyboard logic; do the same here (or store a resolved direction in context) instead of treating Auto as LTR.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1Glg | reply=3350449615 | crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:782
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject blank edit commits instead of deleting tags**

When a user clears the inline edit field and presses Enter, this removes the tag even though the editing contract only replaces a tag when the committed value is non-empty, and removal already has separate Delete/Backspace/delete-trigger paths. This makes an accidental blank edit destructive; treat empty commits as rejected/no-op (while still exiting or restoring focus as intended) rather than deleting the chip.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1Glm | reply=3350449621 | crates/ars-components/src/selection/tags_input/mod.rs:1574
**<sub><sub>![P3 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P3-lightgrey?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Omit the hidden input name when unset**

With the default props this renders `name=""` on every hidden input. That differs from the other form-backed components, which omit `HtmlAttr::Name` when no name prop is provided, and it produces invalid/useless form markup for unnamed fields; only set the attribute when `ctx.name` is `Some`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

1032	/// Builds the plan for an [`Event::AddTag`], including the max-reached announcement.
1033	fn add_tag_plan(ctx: &Context, tag: &str) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {
1034	    let trimmed = tag.trim().to_string();
1035	
1036	    if trimmed.is_empty() {
1037	        return None;
1038	    }
1039	
1040	    if let Some(max) = ctx.max.filter(|&max| ctx.value.get().len() >= max) {
1041	        let announcement = (ctx.messages.max_reached_announcement)(max, &ctx.locale);
1042	
1043	        return Some(
1044	            TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
1045	                ctx.live_message = announcement;
1046	            })
1047	            .with_effect(PendingEffect::named(Effect::Announce)),
1048	        );
1049	    }
1050	
1051	    if !ctx.allow_duplicates && ctx.value.get().contains(&trimmed) {
1052	        return None;
1053	    }
1054	
1055	    if exceeds_max_length(ctx.max_length, &trimmed) {
1056	        return None;
1057	    }
1058	
1059	    Some(
1060	        TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
1061	            let mut tags = ctx.value.get().clone();
1062	
1063	            tags.push(trimmed);
1064	
1065	            ctx.value.set(tags);
1066	            ctx.input_value.clear();
1067	            ctx.focused_tag = None;
1068	        })
1069	        .with_effect(value_change_effect()),

1074	/// Unicode scalar values, matching the browser `maxlength` semantics closely

1076	fn exceeds_max_length(max_length: Option<usize>, value: &str) -> bool {
1077	    max_length.is_some_and(|limit| value.chars().count() > limit)

  "new_string": "/// Builds the plan for an [`Event::AddTag`], including the max-reached announcement.\n///\n/// Mutations build from [`Bindable::pending`] (the staged internal value) rather\n/// than [`Bindable::get`] so that, in controlled mode, successive edits accumulate\n/// instead of each starting from the parent's not-yet-round-tripped value.\nfn add_tag_plan(ctx: &Context, tag: &str) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {\n    let trimmed = tag.trim().to_string();\n\n    if trimmed.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    if let Some(max) = ctx.max.filter(|&max| ctx.value.pending().len() >= max) {\n        let announcement = (ctx.messages.max_reached_announcement)(max, &ctx.locale);\n\n        return Some(\n            TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n                ctx.live_message = announcement;\n            })\n            .with_effect(PendingEffect::named(Effect::Announce)),\n        );\n    }\n\n    if !ctx.allow_duplicates && ctx.value.pending().contains(&trimmed) {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    if exceeds_max_length(ctx.max_length, &trimmed) {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    Some(\n        TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n            let mut tags = ctx.value.pending().clone();\n\n            tags.push(trimmed);\n\n            ctx.value.set(tags);\n            ctx.input_value.clear();\n            ctx.focused_tag = None;\n        })\n        .with_effect(value_change_effect()),\n    )\n}"
}

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1oh2 | reply=3350639905 | :1734
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle Tab while a tag is focused**

When a tag has focus and the user presses Tab, this handler falls through to `_ => {}` even though the TagsInput spec says Tab in the focused-tag state should move to the next tag or the input. Because only the focused tag has `tabindex="0"` and the remaining tags are `tabindex="-1"`, relying on the browser default skips the next tag rather than updating `focused_tag` and emitting a focus effect, so keyboard users cannot tab through the tag chips as specified.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1oh6 | reply=3350639912 | :962
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reset edits when controlled tags are replaced**

If a controlled parent replaces the tag currently being edited with another value at the same index, this only exits edit mode when the new list is shorter, so `editing_draft` continues to show the old tag. In that scenario, pressing Enter/Tab later commits the stale draft over the parent's replacement (for example editing `a`, parent syncs `["x"]`, then commit sends the old draft for index 0), so the controlled update can be silently clobbered.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1oh9 | reply=3350639916 | :888
**<sub><sub>![P3 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P3-lightgrey?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Skip value-change effects for empty clear-all**

When the tag list is already empty, `ClearAll` still sets an empty vector and unconditionally emits `ValueChange`. If the clear trigger is invoked in that state, controlled consumers receive an `on_value_change([])` even though the value did not change, unlike the add/paste paths that only fire when they actually append tags; guard this effect on `ctx.value.pending().is_empty()` to avoid redundant parent updates.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1oiC | reply=3350639925 | :72
**<sub><sub>![P3 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P3-lightgrey?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Align RemoveTag docs with duplicate behavior**

The public `RemoveTag(String)` documentation says duplicate values are all removed, but the transition below intentionally removes only the first matching occurrence before delegating to the index-based remover. With `allow_duplicates(true)`, external users dispatching this event by value will leave extra duplicate chips despite the API docs promising otherwise, so either remove all matches here or update the public contract to match the first-occurrence behavior.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
